svg.title: Where to go next: use it, understand it, trust it, extend it
svg.desc: Map of the documents to read after the README, in four lanes. Use it: Install (docs/guide/install.md: which edition, which OS, container or native scanners), then Your first audit (first-audit.md: how to start it, the Phase 0 questions, depths, where the output goes), then Findings and reports (reports.md: finding files, Markdown, HTML and Excel), then Re-scan (rescan.md: Phase 8 verifies fixes with the same scanner digests); Troubleshooting (troubleshooting.md) when something fails. Understand it: How an audit runs (docs/guide/how-it-works.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: the two layers, phases 0 to 8, who does what), then security-audit/SKILL.md, the full procedure, then the reference folder: the standards index (every standard, its version, the citation rule), the threat-intel method (feeds, matching rules, severity floors) and orchestration (the model and effort matrix, subagent prompts). Trust it, the evidence chain: selftest of both editions on every push and pull request on three operating systems and two Python versions (ci.yml), then the offline eval (eval/README.md: detection, edition parity, linter, threat intel, on every push without an API key), then the live benchmark (benchmark/RESULTS.md: real headless audits against the previous version, run by hand, never in CI), then the release gates (release.yml: versions, CHANGELOGs, the selftests and eval again, SHA256SUMS attached). Running alongside: CodeQL on Python and workflows on every push; a weekly scanner pins pull request, smoke-tested and never auto-merged; live threat feeds fetched at audit time, where a failed feed is a stated gap. Extend it: CONTRIBUTING.md (the gates a pull request must pass), then docs/RELEASING.md (CHANGELOG-driven releases, scanner pin updates), then SECURITY.md (private vulnerability reporting). Dashed arrows cross the lanes: Your first audit leads to How an audit runs (why it works this way), Findings and reports leads to the selftest at the start of the evidence chain (how the claims are checked), and RELEASING leads to the release gates, which the tag runs.

g.text: Where to go next: use it, understand it, trust it, extend it
Every box is a real document. Solid arrows are the reading order; dashed arrows lead into the next layer.
